title: Cold open — is the sales plugin only for professional salespeople?
text: People assume the sales plug-in is built for professional sales people with a CRM. It isn't. It's for anyone who needs clients, consultants, freelancers, agency owners. So, who's it actually for? Consultants, freelancers, agency owners,

title: Who it's actually for
text: Builders, people who need clients but never studied pipeline management and never wanted to. Not a big sales team with an administrator, though it handles that, too. It's useful the moment you need to research a prospect, prep a conversation, or follow up after one. Picture a freelancer with one lead they don't know how to work, no CRM, no playbook, no manager looking over their shoulder. That's exactly where this starts. Not a system for people who already have a sales process, a collaborator for people who don't. Research, prep, follow up, pipeline,

title: Five kinds of help
text: Outreach. Five things and probably work you're already doing badly, doing late, or not doing at all. Point it at a company or a person and

title: Research, prep, and follow-up
text: Get a structured briefing back. What they do, recent news, needs you could address, key contacts. It works from public information alone and gets richer once you connect a CRM. For any client conversation, it builds a prep sheet. The relevant contacts, talking points worth raising, questions worth asking. If you've kept notes from before, it weaves those in, too. Hand it your notes after a call and it drafts the follow up. Not a template, a message that references the specific things you discussed and proposes a concrete next step. Even if your pipeline is a spreadsheet or just a list in your head, it helps you see where everything stands, who's waiting on you, and what's gone quiet. You've got a discovery call in an hour with an agency

title: Anchor walkthrough — the Meridian call
text: You barely know. So, you ask, "Research Meridian Design Studio. What they do, who they serve, recent news, and what they might need from someone like me." A minute later, you've got a one-page briefing you can scan in five. You walk in informed instead of improvising, present, not scrambling, because the research is already done. It doesn't sit at the table with you. It got you ready for it. The call ends. While it's fresh, you dump what happened, their timeline, their real concern, who actually decides. 5 minutes of notes captured now instead of forgotten by Friday. From those notes, it drafts a follow-up that hits every point and suggests a logical next step in a warm, professional tone. The email that would have sat on your list for 3 days is done in 5 minutes. Hand it your whole prospect list and ask

title: Managing the pipeline and finding new names
text: The hard questions. Which conversations need a nudge? What's gone cold? Where this week's energy should go? It's like having a sales manager who keeps you honest about follow-through without the awkwardness of actually having one. Need new names? Ask it to scout a market, agencies in a region that might need what you offer, and it comes back with a list that has context, not just company names. You decide who's worth pursuing. And when you reach out cold, it drafts something that references their actual situation and offers a conversation, not a hard sell. Personal enough to feel human, structured enough to say something worth reading. Tell it three things: what you sell, how your process works, who your ideal client is, and it stops guessing and starts sounding like you. Connect to CRM, even a free one, and its research gets richer still, but it isn't required. When you close a deal, tell it what worked, what resonated, which objection came up, what sealed it. Over time, that builds institutional knowledge that sharpens every future suggestion. But don't let it automate the

title: Both directions — what it's not for
text: Relationship. It's excellent at preparation and follow-through, not a replacement for being genuinely present in the conversation. Hand it the admin instead, activity logging, note formatting, follow-up scheduling. The chores you skip when busy, so you can focus on people. And keep your notes current.
